plan: This is the first round, so there's no history to learn from. The optimal strategy in a second-price auction with rational bidders is to bid your true value. This prevents you from losing money by bidding above your value and maximizes your chances of winning when it's profitable. I will bid my value of $31.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with payment equal to the second-highest bid (Vickrey auction variant). My goal is to maximize profit. In this type of auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, as it guarantees I win when my value is highest and never pay more than my value. Since the values are drawn independently each round, past rounds don't influence the current value distribution.

The optimal strategy in a second-price auction is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it maximizes my profit regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding below my value risks losing a profitable item. Bidding above my value risks winning an item for more than it's worth.
